//: THE VERIFIED TIER of the Mochiii MCP marketplace: servers someone writing code in the editor would use --
files, git, GitHub, databases, a browser, docs -- not connectors to SaaS accounts. Each entry was chosen by
a person and is pinned here, in full, by a person: the package, its exact version (an OCI image by its
digest, since a tag can be moved), the arguments after it, and the variables it reads. `npm run mcp:sync`
does NOT move these pins; it only rebuilds the community tier and says when the registry has a newer
version of a verified server. A bump is an edit to this file, then `npm run mcp:handshake`, which starts
the new pin and records its tools/list -- the build refuses a verified entry with no passing record.
`namespace` is the server's name in the official MCP Registry, where the registry lists it; the MCP
project's own reference servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory, sequential-thinking) are not there.
`env` lists variables by NAME only: Mochiii passes them through, never stores a value in a catalog.
`cwd: workspace` starts the server in the project; without it a server gets a private folder of its own.
Filesystem, git and fetch overlap Mochiii's own confined tools. They were left out until 2026-10-26 and
are offered now because people ask for them by name; the add flow still makes the user acknowledge that
the server runs unconfined, and filesystem and git start in the project only. postgres and sqlite are Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases: the MCP project's
own postgres server is deprecated on npm and had a read-only bypass, and its sqlite server is archived.
The cloud and vendor servers from aws-documentation on were added 2026-11-03. Each is the vendor's own package
(AWS Labs for AWS), and each was started through Mochiii (mochiii mcp add, then mochiii mcp check) on a throwaway
HOME with no real credential -- a required key got a placeholder. azure-mcp and angular-cli need Node.js 22 or
later, so their handshakes were run on Node 22.23.4; every other record is from the runtime handshakes.json names.
Where a third-party community listing already held the bare name (azure, supabase, sentry, grafana and others),
the id is the vendor's server name with -mcp: ids are shared with community.json and must not repeat.

servers.name: Filesystem
servers.description: Read, write, move and search files in the open project, from the MCP reference servers. Reaches only the project folder it starts in.

servers.name: Git
servers.description: Status, diff, log, branches and commits in the project's Git repository, from the MCP reference servers.

servers.name: GitHub
servers.description: GitHub's official server: repositories, issues, pull requests, code search and Actions, through your own token.

env.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A GitHub personal access token. Scope it to what you want Mochiii to reach.

servers.name: PostgreSQL
servers.description: Run SQL against a PostgreSQL database and inspect its schema, tables and indexes. Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases, with its prebuilt PostgreSQL tools.

env.name: POSTGRES_HOST
env.description: The database host, e.g. localhost.

env.name: POSTGRES_PORT
env.description: The database port, usually 5432.

env.name: POSTGRES_DATABASE
env.description: The database to connect to.

env.name: POSTGRES_USER
env.description: The user to connect as. A read-only role is the safe choice.

env.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env.description: That user's password.

servers.name: SQLite
servers.description: Query a SQLite database file and inspect its tables. Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases, with its prebuilt SQLite tools, started in the project.

env.name: SQLITE_DATABASE
env.description: Path to the database file, relative to the project or absolute.

servers.name: Playwright
servers.description: Drive a real browser with Playwright: navigate, click, fill forms and read pages through the accessibility tree.

servers.name: Chrome DevTools
servers.description: Inspect and debug a live Chrome: network requests, console, performance traces and DOM, from the Chrome DevTools team.

servers.name: Fetch
servers.description: Fetch a web page or API response and hand it to the model as Markdown, from the MCP reference servers. It can reach any URL your machine can, local ones included.

servers.name: Context7
servers.description: Up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples for libraries, pulled into the model's context on request.

env.name: CONTEXT7_API_KEY
env.description: A Context7 API key, for higher rate limits. It works without one.

servers.name: ESLint
servers.description: Lint files in the project with its own ESLint configuration and explain the problems found. The ESLint team's official server.

servers.name: Next.js DevTools
servers.description: Next.js documentation, upgrade guides and a running dev server's errors and routes, from the Next.js team.

servers.name: Nx
servers.description: Understand an Nx monorepo: its projects, their dependencies, targets and generators, and the Nx docs. From the Nx team.

servers.name: MongoDB
servers.description: Query and manage a MongoDB database: collections, documents, indexes and aggregations. MongoDB's official server.

env.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING
env.description: The connection string of the database to work with. Without it, the model has to be given one with the connect tool.

env.name: MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY
env.description: Set to true to allow only reads.

servers.name: Redis
servers.description: Read, write and search data in Redis, from Redis's official server. Connects to localhost:6379 unless told otherwise.

env.name: REDIS_HOST
env.description: The Redis host, if not localhost.

env.name: REDIS_PORT
env.description: The Redis port, if not 6379.

env.name: REDIS_USERNAME
env.description: The user to connect as, if any.

env.name: REDIS_PWD
env.description: The password, if any.

servers.name: Terraform
servers.description: Terraform Registry providers, modules and policies, for writing accurate Terraform, and HCP Terraform workspaces with a token. Runs Terraform operations only if you enable them yourself.

env.name: TFE_TOKEN
env.description: An HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise token, for workspace tools. Registry lookups work without it.

env.name: TFE_ADDRESS
env.description: Your Terraform Enterprise URL, if you do not use HCP Terraform.

servers.name: Memory
servers.description: A persistent knowledge graph the model can write to and recall from across conversations: decisions, conventions, what a module is for. An MCP reference server.

env.name: MEMORY_FILE_PATH
env.description: Where to keep the knowledge graph. Set it, or the graph may not outlive a package cache clean.

servers.name: Sequential Thinking
servers.description: A structured tool for step-by-step problem solving that can revise and branch its own reasoning. An MCP reference server.

servers.name: AWS Documentation
servers.description: Search and read the AWS documentation and get related pages, from AWS Labs. Needs no AWS account.

env.name: AWS_DOCUMENTATION_PARTITION
env.description: Set to aws-cn for the AWS China documentation.

servers.name: AWS API
servers.description: Can create, change and delete AWS resources. Run AWS CLI commands against your account, and get the command for a task described in words, from AWS Labs. Uses your AWS credentials.

env.name: AWS_API_MCP_PROFILE_NAME
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1.

env.name: READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY
env.description: Set to true to allow only read operations.

servers.name: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
servers.description: Find your Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and query them in plain language, from AWS Labs. Uses your AWS credentials.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
servers.description: Can create, change and delete AgentCore resources. Create and manage Amazon Bedrock AgentCore resources (runtimes, gateways, memory, identity) and search the AgentCore docs, from AWS Labs. Offers over a hundred tools.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: AWS Infrastructure as Code
servers.description: Validate CloudFormation templates, check them for compliance, troubleshoot failed deployments and search the CloudFormation and CDK docs, from AWS Labs.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: AWS Pricing
servers.description: Look up current AWS prices by service and Region and estimate what an architecture will cost, from AWS Labs. Uses your AWS credentials.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: Amazon CloudWatch
servers.description: Read CloudWatch metrics, alarms and logs and run Logs Insights queries to find the cause of a problem, from AWS Labs.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: Amazon DynamoDB
servers.description: DynamoDB data-modeling guidance, model validation, cost analysis and code generation, from AWS Labs.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: AWS Serverless
servers.description: Can create, change and delete AWS resources. Build, deploy and troubleshoot serverless applications with AWS SAM and Lambda, with guidance on serverless patterns, from AWS Labs. Building and deploying needs the AWS SAM CLI.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: Amazon EKS
servers.description: Can create, change and delete cluster and Kubernetes resources. Inspect, manage and troubleshoot EKS clusters and their Kubernetes resources, from AWS Labs. Needs a Region set.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1.

servers.name: AWS IAM
servers.description: Can create, change and delete IAM users, roles, groups, policies and access keys; each write asks to be confirmed first. Review IAM users, roles, groups and policies and simulate what a policy allows, from AWS Labs.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.description: The profile in ~/.aws to use, if not the default one.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.description: The AWS Region to work in, such as us-east-1. Otherwise the profile's own.

servers.name: Azure
servers.description: Can create, change and delete Azure resources. Microsoft's Azure MCP Server: storage, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, AKS, App Service, monitoring and more across your subscriptions, through your Azure sign-in. Needs Node.js 22 or later.

env.name: AZURE_TENANT_ID
env.description: With the next two, sign in as a service principal instead of through the Azure CLI.

env.name: AZURE_CLIENT_ID
env.description: The service principal's application (client) ID.

env.name: AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: The service principal's client secret.

env.name: AZURE_MCP_COLLECT_TELEMETRY
env.description: Set to false to turn off Microsoft's usage telemetry.

servers.name: MarkItDown
servers.description: Turn a PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, an image or a web page into Markdown the model can read, from Microsoft's MarkItDown. A pre-release.

servers.name: Google Cloud Observability
servers.description: Read Cloud Logging entries, Cloud Monitoring metrics and alerts, traces and Error Reporting in your Google Cloud projects. Uses your Application Default Credentials.

servers.name: Google Cloud Storage
servers.description: Can create, overwrite and delete buckets and objects. List, read, write and manage Cloud Storage buckets and objects in your Google Cloud projects. Uses your Application Default Credentials.

env.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
env.description: The project to work in, if not your gcloud default.

servers.name: Cloud Run
servers.description: Can create projects and deploy and change services. Deploy a folder or a container image to Cloud Run, and list your services and read their logs. Uses your Application Default Credentials.

env.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
env.description: The project to deploy to, if not your gcloud default.

env.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION
env.description: The region to deploy to, such as europe-west1.

servers.name: Firebase
servers.description: Can create projects and apps, change settings and deploy. Firebase's server, from the Firebase CLI: projects and apps, Firestore, Authentication, Data Connect, Storage, security rules and more. Starts in the project; sign in with firebase login.

servers.name: Angular CLI
servers.description: Can run the project's build, test and dev-server targets. The Angular CLI's server: search the Angular docs and examples, get current best practices and inspect the project's workspace. Starts in the project. Needs Node.js 22 or later.

servers.name: Supabase
servers.description: Can create, change and delete projects, data, migrations and functions. Supabase's server: projects, tables, SQL, migrations, logs, Edge Functions, branches and the Supabase docs, through your personal access token.

env.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A Supabase personal access token, from your account's Access Tokens page.

servers.name: Sentry
servers.description: Can resolve, assign and update issues and manage projects and teams. Sentry's server: look up issues, errors and stack traces, releases and performance data in your Sentry organization.

env.name: SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A Sentry user auth token.

env.name: SENTRY_HOST
env.description: Your self-hosted Sentry's host name, if not sentry.io.

servers.name: Netlify
servers.description: Can create, change and deploy sites. Netlify's server: create, build and deploy sites and manage their environment variables, forms and extensions through the Netlify API and CLI. Starts in the project.

env.name: NETLIFY_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A Netlify personal access token, if the server's own sign-in does not work for you.

servers.name: Heroku
servers.description: Can create, change, scale and restart apps, add-ons and databases. Heroku's server: apps, dynos, add-ons, Postgres, pipelines and logs. Needs the Heroku CLI (10.8.1 or later) installed.

env.name: HEROKU_API_KEY
env.description: A Heroku API key, or the token heroku authorizations:create gives you.

servers.name: Postman
servers.description: Can create and change collections, environments, mocks, specs and workspaces. Postman's server: workspaces, collections, requests, environments, mocks and API specs in your Postman account.

env.name: POSTMAN_API_KEY
env.description: A Postman API key, from your account settings.

servers.name: Snyk
servers.description: Snyk's server, from the Snyk CLI: scan the project's code, open-source dependencies, containers and infrastructure as code for vulnerabilities. Starts in the project.

env.name: SNYK_TOKEN
env.description: A Snyk API token. Without it, sign in with the server's own auth tool.

servers.name: Shopify Dev
servers.description: Shopify's developer server: search the shopify.dev docs, explore the Admin GraphQL schema and validate GraphQL and theme code. Needs no Shopify account.

servers.name: MUI
servers.description: MUI's server: answers from the official Material UI and MUI X documentation, with real links, so generated code matches the library.

servers.name: Prisma
servers.description: Can change your development database's schema. The Prisma CLI's local server: check migration status, create and apply migrations in development and open Prisma Studio, in the project.

servers.name: DigitalOcean
servers.description: Can create, change and delete DigitalOcean resources. DigitalOcean's server: App Platform, Droplets, databases, Kubernetes, networking, Spaces and more, through your API token. Offers several hundred tools.

env.name: DIGITALOCEAN_API_TOKEN
env.description: A DigitalOcean personal access token. Scope it to what you want Mochiii to reach.

servers.name: ClickHouse
servers.description: Read-only unless you set CLICKHOUSE_ALLOW_WRITE_ACCESS to true; then it can create tables and insert rows. ClickHouse's server: list databases and tables and run SQL on a ClickHouse server.

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_HOST
env.description: The ClickHouse server's host name.

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_USER
env.description: The user to connect as.

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
env.description: That user's password.

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_PORT
env.description: The port, if not 8443 (or 8123 without TLS).

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_SECURE
env.description: Set to false to connect without TLS.

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_ALLOW_WRITE_ACCESS
env.description: Set to true to allow writes such as CREATE and INSERT. Without it, queries are read-only.

env.name: CLICKHOUSE_ALLOW_DROP
env.description: With write access on, set to true to also allow DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE and UPDATE.

servers.name: Grafana
servers.description: Can create, change and delete dashboards, alerts, annotations and other Grafana resources. Grafana's server: search dashboards, query Prometheus and Loki data sources, and work with alerts and incidents in your Grafana.

env.name: GRAFANA_URL
env.description: Your Grafana's address, such as http://localhost:3000.

env.name: GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN
env.description: A Grafana service account token. Or set the username and password below.

env.name: GRAFANA_USERNAME
env.description: A Grafana user, if not using a token.

env.name: GRAFANA_PASSWORD
env.description: That user's password.

servers.name: Vault
servers.description: Can create, change and delete secrets, mounts and PKI roles. HashiCorp's Vault server: list, read and write secrets in KV mounts and manage mounts and PKI in your Vault.

env.name: VAULT_ADDR
env.description: Your Vault's address, such as https://vault.example.com:8200.

env.name: VAULT_TOKEN
env.description: A Vault token. Give it a policy limited to what you want Mochiii to reach.

env.name: VAULT_NAMESPACE
env.description: The Vault Enterprise namespace, if any.

servers.name: SonarQube
servers.description: Can change the status of issues and security hotspots. SonarSource's server: issues, security hotspots, quality gates and code analysis from SonarQube Cloud or SonarQube Server.

env.name: SONARQUBE_TOKEN
env.description: A SonarQube user token.

env.name: SONARQUBE_ORG
env.description: Your SonarQube Cloud organization key. Set it, or the server has to look it up with the token.

env.name: SONARQUBE_URL
env.description: Your SonarQube Server's address, if you do not use SonarQube Cloud.
